text:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up: proposing a 'handoff' pattern — stream-first with short-lived handoff tokens so SDKs can switch from streaming to polling on disconnect. Thoughts?

maria: +1 to stream-first. can you sketch how the handoff token looks? expiration, single-use? :thinking_face:

alex: single-use-ish. token encodes session id + resume offset + backend variant. short TTL (30s) to avoid long-lived state. if token expired, fall back to new request with idempotency key.

cheng: Main UX question: do we expose the token to app authors or keep it internal to the SDK? exposing simplifies advanced use (manual reconnect) but raises surface area.

sophie: prefer SDK-managed. most apps just want "restore()" on a stream object. exposing token is ok as opt-in for advanced cases.

alex: +1. SDK-managed by default, opt-in .handoffToken for advanced ops. Also need consistent retry semantics across python/ts/go: if stream fails mid-request, SDK should attempt streaming reconnect up to N times with increasing backoff, then use handoff token to fetch missing chunks via polling.

maria: Are we aligning with existing retry semantics for REST calls? e.g., idempotency-key only used for non-stream requests. mixing both might confuse.

alex: plan: keep idempotency-key for single-call semantics. handoff token is strictly for streaming continuity (it can include an idempotency reference but used differently). document both in SDK retry page.

cheng: Implementation detail for Go: gRPC stream vs http2/eventsource differences. We should unify via a TransportAdapter interface:

```go
// pseudo
type TransportAdapter interface {
  Stream(ctx context.Context, req *Request) (StreamHandle, error)
  Poll(ctx context.Context, token string) (PollResult, error)
}
```

and then have HttpAdapter / GrpcAdapter implement it. keeps SDK logic shared.

alex: yep. TS/Python mirror the same surface. in TS:

```ts
const session = client.startStream({ model: 'x' })
try {
  for await (const chunk of session) {
    onChunk(chunk)
  }
} catch (err) {
  // sdk tries reconnect using handoff token, otherwise returns error
  await session.restore()
}
```

sophie: restore() ergonomics: return boolean for success or throw error? in python maybe `bool` is ok, TS prefer throw. pick one?

maria: ergonomics per language: python returns True/False, ts/go throw on failure. but ensure docs clearly show parity and examples.

alex: agree. important tradeoffs section to include in RFC follow-up:
- security: handoff tokens short-lived + bound to client IP/region when possible
- observability: log token issuance and restore attempts with sampling
- cost: polling fallback might increase token count — add server-side rate limits per session
- complexity: TransportAdapter centralizes complexity but increases test surface

cheng: small nit: what happens to partial events ordering across stream -> poll boundary? We must guarantee ordering by sequencing at token level (seq numbers). SDK should stitch chunks and drop duplicates.

alex: yes: token includes next_seq. server guarantees monotonic seq. SDK dedups by seq. I'll add a minimal protocol section.

maria: sounds good. next steps: alex to write short follow-up RFC with protocol sketch + code examples per language, assign reviewers: @cheng, @sophie. deploy-bot: please add an item to eng-platform backlog?

deploy-bot: [automated] created ticket ENG-7421 "handoff transport: RFC + SDK prototypes" and assigned to alex, cheng, sophie. :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks. I'll post a draft by EOD tomorrow and include perf probes for stream->poll path.

sophie: 👍 also add a small test harness to simulate flaky networks (chaos) so we can iterate on backoff params.

maria: and add a short note on how this interacts with rollout policies (dedicated vs hosted) — some customers might prefer polling-only for compliance.

alex: will do. thanks all.
